title: Injectivity and kernel image of the ideal homology cycle map
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal, $M$ an $R$-module and $P$ a projective resolution of $M$ with free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Put $C=P\otimes_R R/I$. Let $\mu:I\otimes_R M\to M$ be $R$-linear with $\mu(a\otimes x)=ax$. Suppose $\delta_H:H_1(C)\to I\otimes_R M$ is $R$-linear and satisfies the following formula: for every cycle $z$, lift $y\in P_1$ with $z=y\otimes1$ and every finite expression $d_1y=\sum_j a_jp_j$, its value on $[z]$ is $\sum_j a_j\otimes\epsilon(p_j)$. Then $\delta_H$ is injective and its image is $\ker\mu$. This statement assumes the formula, not the existence of such a map.

source.place: Parent ideal-kernel naturality node, Steps 1–3; Stacks Algebra, proof of Tag 00M5 and Remark 00M6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M6).

proof.text: Use exists_quotient_cycle_lift to write each degree-one quotient cycle as y tensor 1 with d y = sum a_j p_j. The homology projection is surjective. The assumed formula, linearity of multiplication and augmentation, and complex_d_comp_π_f_zero give mu delta_H = 0 on every homology class.

source.place: Parent ideal-kernel naturality node, Steps 1–3; Stacks Algebra, proof of Tag 00M5 and Remark 00M6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M6).

proof.text: Let epsilon be the degree-zero augmentation and d the degree-one differential. ProjectiveResolution.exact₀ gives Function.Exact d epsilon and the augmentation is surjective. Apply lTensor_exact I to get exactness of I tensor P_1 -> I tensor P_0 -> I tensor M. Construct m_n:I tensor P_n -> P_n as tensoring the ideal inclusion followed by TensorProduct.lid; on a tensor it is a p. Tensor induction proves epsilon m_0 = mu (I tensor epsilon), d m_1 = m_0 (I tensor d), and m_n(s) tensor 1 = 0 modulo I.

source.place: Parent ideal-kernel naturality node, Steps 1–3; Stacks Algebra, proof of Tag 00M5 and Remark 00M6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M6).

proof.text: For a cycle with lift y and expression d y = sum a_j p_j, suppose sum a_j tensor epsilon(p_j) = 0. Put t=sum a_j tensor p_j. Tensor right exactness provides s in I tensor P_1 with (I tensor d)(s)=t. Then y-m_1(s) is an actual cycle. ProjectiveResolution.exact_succ 0 provides w in P_2 with d_2 w=y-m_1(s). As m_1(s) tensor 1=0, the original quotient cycle is toCycles(w tensor 1), so its homology class is zero by toCycles_comp_homologyπ. Apply the assumed formula to a representative of any class killed by delta_H. This proves a trivial kernel, and linearity applied to x-y proves injectivity.

source.place: Parent ideal-kernel naturality node, Steps 1–3; Stacks Algebra, proof of Tag 00M5 and Remark 00M6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M6).

proof.text: For t in ker mu, LinearMap.lTensor_surjective lifts t to s in I tensor P_0. The identity epsilon m_0=mu (I tensor epsilon) implies epsilon(m_0(s))=0. Resolution exactness in degree zero gives y with d y=m_0(s). TensorProduct.exists_sum_tmul_eq gives s=sum a_j tensor p_j, hence d y=sum a_j p_j. The vanishing of m_0(s) modulo I makes y tensor 1 a quotient cycle, constructed with cyclesMk. The assumed formula sends its homology class to (I tensor epsilon)(s)=t. Combine this kernel-to-range inclusion with the first step to prove the range equality.

theorem tor_ideal_homology_exactness
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (P : ProjectiveResolution M) (hP : ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Free R (P.complex.X n))
    (μR : (I ⊗[R] M) →ₗ[R] M)
    (hμR : ∀ (a : I) (x : M), μR (a ⊗ₜ[R] x) = (a : R) • x)
    (δH : ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).homology 1 →ₗ[R] (I ⊗[R] M))
    (hδH : ∀ (z : ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸
        I))).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).cycles 1)
        (y : P.complex.X 1) (k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → I) (p : Fin k → P.complex.X 0),
        ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).iCycles 1 z = y ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ I) →
        P.complex.d 1 0 y = ∑ j, (a j : R) • p j →
        δH
          (((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).homologyπ 1 z) =
          ∑ j, a j ⊗ₜ[R] P.π.f 0 (p j)) :
    Function.Injective δH ∧ LinearMap.range δH = LinearMap.ker μR
